question.text: Which will occur next with respect to the FDA's review of deramiocel for muscular dystrophy?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as the next of the listed events occurring after October 31, 2026 with respect to the FDA's review of deramiocel for Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
question.fine_print: Please note that the option for "FDA approval" is for any approval, including accelerated approval or emergency use authorization. Permission solely for clinical trials or expanded access does not count.

research:
Capricor's application for deramiocel is still pending. The FDA's decision deadline (PDUFA date) is **November 22, 2026**, a Sunday, one day before this question resolves on November 23. As of October 28 I found no approval, no new complete response letter (CRL, the FDA's formal rejection) and no report of label talks. Nothing has settled the question yet.

### 1. Resolution source
- No URL is given in the criteria. The deciding sources would be a Capricor press release or 8-K filing, or an FDA action, announcing approval or a CRL.
- 2026-08-24: The background article says the FDA accepted extra HOPE-3 trial data as a "major amendment" to the application. That pushed the deadline from Aug 22 to Nov 22, 2026. Capricor asked for a narrower indication focused on upper-limb function. [CGTLive](https://www.cgtlive.com/view/fda-extends-deramiocel-review-dmd)
- 2026-10-28: The latest status is still "under review, PDUFA date Nov 22, 2026." [pdufa.bio](https://www.pdufa.bio/pdufa/CAPR-deramiocel)

### 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The decision is due Nov 22. Because that is a Sunday, the FDA may act on Friday Nov 20 or earlier. I could not confirm FDA weekend practice for this case.
- I found no reported late-cycle meeting or labeling talks for this review round. In the company's briefing document for the July advisory committee, Capricor said labeling discussions had not yet happened. [FDA doc](https://www.fda.gov/media/193840/download)

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-10-21: CAPR stock fell 11% that day. It was down about 38% for October and about 80% year-to-date. Earlier in October, H.C. Wainwright said rejection was more likely than approval. Roth floated the idea of a second advisory panel on upper-limb function. [Stocktwits](https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/capr-stock-on-track-for-worst-month-since-july-ad-com-vote-on-deramiocel-as-november-fda-decision-nears/cZxMfqVRBvy)
- 2026-10-05: At the World Muscle Society Congress, Capricor presented results from the HOPE-3 open-label extension. Patients who switched from placebo had 76% slower upper-limb decline than in their placebo year. These were descriptive analyses with no statistical testing, and the data are part of the amendment. [GlobeNewswire](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/10/05/3374601/0/en/capricor-therapeutics-presents-positive-hope-3-open-label-extension-data-on-upper-limb-function-in-duchenne-muscular-dystrophy-at-2026-world-muscle-society-congress.html)
- 2026-08-24: The FDA extended the deadline to Nov 22. Capricor said the FDA cited the large unmet need in Duchenne. [StockTitan 8-K](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/CAPR/8-k-capricor-therapeutics-inc-reports-material-event-b9849b36815b.html), [BioPharm Intl](https://www.biopharminternational.com/view/fda-extends-deramiocel-pdufa-date-to-november-2026-after-capricor-submits-refined-dmd-indication)
- 2026-08-13: In its Q2 report, Capricor said it planned to file the amendment and had about $238M in cash. [SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001133869/000110465926095908/capr-20260813xex99d1.htm)
- 2026-07-29: The FDA's cell and gene therapy advisory committee voted 9 to 3 that the evidence did not support effectiveness for cardiomyopathy. The FDA's briefing document concluded efficacy was not shown, although HOPE-3 met its PUL 2.0 primary endpoint (p=0.029). [NeurologyLive](https://www.neurologylive.com/view/fda-advisory-committee-votes-against-deramiocel-dmd-cardiomyopathy), [FDA Law Blog](https://www.thefdalawblog.com/2026/08/the-fda-adcomm-reboot-part-1-lessons-from-the-meeting-on-capricors-deramiocel/)
- 2026-03: The FDA accepted the resubmission after the first CRL as a Class 2 resubmission, with an Aug 22 deadline. [PPMD](https://www.parentprojectmd.org/deramiocel-where-we-are-today/)
- 2025-07: First CRL, citing lack of substantial evidence of effectiveness and manufacturing (CMC) questions. [CGTLive](https://www.cgtlive.com/view/capricor-bla-dmd-cardiomyopathy-cell-therapy-deramiocel-slammed-crl)

### 4. Base rates
- I found no formal statistic for this situation. Two qualitative points:
  - The FDA usually acts on or before its deadline. When the deadline falls on a weekend, the action often comes the previous business day. Missed deadlines do happen, and CBER (the FDA center reviewing this cell therapy) has missed some recently, but I could not find data on how often.
  - Approval after a negative advisory vote plus a negative FDA briefing document is relatively uncommon. Duchenne is an exception: it has precedents of flexible or accelerated approvals, such as Elevidys and the exon-skipping drugs.
- This product has already received one CRL (July 2025).
- A third deadline extension is possible but rare. The FDA normally allows only one three-month extension for a major amendment per review cycle.

### 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on deramiocel. None of the markets supplied with the question match it; they cover other drugs (CagriSema, retatrutide, Venglustat and others) and macro events.
- Analyst views: H.C. Wainwright sees rejection as more likely. Of 10 analysts in the Koyfin consensus, 4 rate the stock Buy and 6 Hold, with a $27 average price target. The roughly 80% stock decline this year suggests the market expects a negative outcome. [Stocktwits](https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/capr-stock-on-track-for-worst-month-since-july-ad-com-vote-on-deramiocel-as-november-fda-decision-nears/cZxMfqVRBvy)

### 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Early to mid November 2026: Capricor's Q3 earnings report and call, date not confirmed. It may give regulatory hints such as label talks, inspection status or a late-cycle meeting.
- Up to Nov 20-22, 2026: The FDA action itself, either approval (possibly accelerated, on the upper-limb indication) or a CRL.
- Edge cases for the "Neither" option:
  - The FDA misses the deadline.
  - Capricor discloses the decision only after Nov 23.
  - The FDA calls a second advisory committee, as Roth suggested, which would likely push the timeline back.
- Event between Oct 28 and Oct 31: I found no sign of an early action. If one happened, it would fall before the question's window, which only counts events after Oct 31.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** About 3.5 weeks. The PDUFA date is Sunday, November 22, 2026, so the FDA will likely act by Friday, November 20. The question closes November 23.

(b) **Status quo:** The application is under review. The default path is an FDA action on or just before the deadline. Given the negative advisory committee vote and the negative FDA briefing document, the default action looks more like a complete response letter (CRL) than an approval.

(c) **Base rates:**
- The FDA acts on or before its PDUFA date roughly 85-90% of the time. CBER has missed some dates recently, so I use about 80-85% for this case.
- Approval after a negative advisory vote combined with a negative FDA briefing document is uncommon, perhaps 20-30% of cases.
- Duchenne has a record of regulatory flexibility, for example Elevidys and the exon-skipping drugs. That raises the approval chance somewhat.
- This product has already received one CRL, in July 2025.

(d) **Strongest evidence:**
- July 29, 2026: the advisory committee voted 9 to 3 that effectiveness was not supported for cardiomyopathy. The FDA's briefing document concluded efficacy was not shown, although HOPE-3 met its PUL 2.0 primary endpoint (p=0.029).
- August 24, 2026: the FDA accepted a major amendment that narrowed the indication to upper-limb function. It extended the deadline to November 22 and cited the high unmet need. This shows some engagement, a modest positive.
- October 5, 2026: open-label extension data were presented. They were descriptive only, with no statistical testing.
- October 2026: the stock fell about 38% for the month and about 80% year to date. H.C. Wainwright said rejection was more likely. Roth raised the possibility of a second advisory panel.
- As of the company's July briefing, no labeling discussions had been reported.

(e) **Unexpected scenario:** The FDA could grant accelerated approval for the narrowed upper-limb indication, citing unmet need and Duchenne precedent, with a confirmatory study required. Alternatively, CBER could miss the date or schedule a second advisory committee, which would push the action past November 23 and resolve "Neither."

**How I got the numbers:** I put the chance of an action before November 23 at about 82%. Conditional on action, I put the chance of a CRL at about 67% and approval at about 33%. Starting from the roughly 25% base rate for approval after negative reviews, I moved approval up slightly because of the narrowed indication and Duchenne flexibility. I moved it back down because of the market pessimism and the lack of any reported labeling talks. That gives roughly 27% approval, 56% CRL and 17% neither.

Option_A: 0.27
Option_B: 0.56
Option_C: 0.17

(a) **Time left:** The PDUFA date is Sunday, November 22, 2026, and the question resolves November 23. That leaves about 3.5 weeks. Action is most likely between November 18 and 22, possibly on Friday, November 20.

(b) **Status quo:** The application is still under review with no action. If nothing changed, "Neither" would win. However, a PDUFA date falls inside the window, so the default expectation is that the FDA acts.

(c) **Base rates:**
- The FDA meets roughly 90% of PDUFA goal dates. CBER has had more misses recently, and labeling or inspection delays sometimes push action past the date. I put "no action disclosed by November 23" at roughly 12-18%.
- Approval after a negative advisory committee vote combined with a negative FDA briefing document typically runs about 20-30%.
- Duchenne has unusual regulatory flexibility. Elevidys and the exon-skipping drugs were approved despite reviewer skepticism.

(d) **Strongest evidence:**
- July 29, 2026: The advisory committee voted 9-3 against effectiveness, and the FDA's briefing document concluded efficacy was not shown. This is a strong negative.
- August 24, 2026: The FDA accepted a major amendment with a narrower upper-limb indication, cited unmet need, and extended the review rather than issuing a CRL. This is a modest positive and suggests openness to a path forward.
- October 5, 2026: The open-label extension data on upper-limb function are only descriptive. This is a weak positive.
- October 2026: The stock fell about 38% in the month and about 80% year to date, and H.C. Wainwright called rejection more likely. The market expects a CRL.
- There are no reports of labeling discussions, which is mildly negative for approval.
- HOPE-3 did meet its primary endpoint (p=0.029). That supports a regulatory-flexibility approval under a Duchenne-friendly framing.

(e) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- The FDA grants accelerated approval on upper-limb function despite the advisory vote, citing the HOPE-3 primary endpoint and unmet need.
- Alternatively, CBER misses the date or convenes a second advisory committee, as Roth floated, and "Neither" wins.
- A late disclosure after November 23 would also push the result to "Neither."

**Reasoning:** I start with about 85% that the FDA acts and Capricor discloses it by November 22-23. Given action, I put approval at about 33%. That is slightly above the base rate for a negative advisory vote, because the FDA chose to extend the review rather than reject outright and because of Duchenne precedents. It is tempered by the negative briefing document and the market's pessimism. That gives roughly 0.28 approval, 0.56 CRL and 0.16 neither.

Option_A: 0.28
Option_B: 0.56
Option_C: 0.16

(c) **Base rates:**

(d) **Strongest evidence:**

  - Jul 29, 2026: The advisory committee voted 9 to 3 against effectiveness for cardiomyopathy, and the FDA briefing document said efficacy was not shown.
  - Jul 2025: The first CRL cited both efficacy and manufacturing (CMC) issues.

- A Sunday action is disclosed only on November 23, which creates resolution ambiguity.

**Reasoning:** I started from about a 75/25 CRL/approval split, conditional on the FDA acting. I moved approval up modestly because the primary endpoint was met, the indication was narrowed and the FDA framed the extension around unmet need. I kept CRL dominant because of the panel vote, the briefing document and the market signal. I then put about 17% on "Neither" to cover a missed deadline, a second panel or timing ambiguity.

I moved slightly up from the bare post-negative-panel base rate because of the Duchenne precedent, the met primary endpoint and the FDA's willingness to extend. That is offset by the market's strong pessimism and the absence of reported label talks.
